paragraphs: Validate QE bulk and vacancy benchmarks.
-    Compare QE and DFTpy vacancy energetics.
-     Separate numerical convergence from method limitation.
Gillan 1989: relaxed Al vacancy ≈ 0.56 eV; experiment ≈ 0.66 eV.

- Primitive fcc Al bulk cell: 1 atom.
- EOS scan: 9 points from a0 = 4.000 to 4.080 A.
- ecut scan: 300-1000 eV at fixed 16x16x16.
- High-k check extended to 20, 24, 30, 40, 60, 80.
Important: n×n×n means primitive-cell replication, not volume in Å³.
DFTpy status and supercell notation caveat
- Primitive-cell size scan completed: 4×4×4 to 14×14×14.- All DFTpy vacancy relaxations reached fmax < 0.02 eV/A.
Results : QE vacancy convergence and Gillan benchmark
Cutoff effect is negligible above 400 eV.

- KEDF: TFvW- Pseudopotential: BLPS local Al recpot- XC: PBE-GGA- Geometry: primitive FCC supercells- Lattice constant fixed to QE a0 for direct comparison- Vacancy: one central Al atom removed- Relaxation target: fmax < 0.02 eV/Å
Therefore, the high DFTpy value is not caused by insufficient supercell size.
DFTpy / TFvW gives a numerically stable but systematically higher vacancy formation energy:
DFTpy ≈ 2.9–3.2 eV, while QE ≈ 0.57–0.62 eV and literature / experiment ≈ 0.56–0.66 eV.
Bulk Convergence: 80×80×80 k-mesh validates that 40×40×40 is sufficient.
Vacancy Formation (QE): 0.5725 eV, closely matching Gillan 1989 (0.56 eV).
DFTpy Stability: Vacancy energy is stable at ~2.94 eV across both grid spacing and supercell size scans (up to 14×14×14).
Key Insight: Discrepancy is attributed to functional limitations (TFvW) rather than numerical parameters (spacing/size).
